subject: Re: Encord <> Troveo Partnership Introduction
text:
Hi @Roger Liang <roger@encord.com>,

Circling back on the customer's ask, please see this *sheet
<https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HYPLF1n1Q1M0YK-yyQIpc6EfU3SJ8crey73mpyDxjfw/edit?usp=sharing>
*for
our estimated volumes across the categories you mentioned, as well as some
sample links for calibration. In terms of clarifying questions, it would be
very helpful to know:

   - The overarching use case(s) the customer is training for so that we
   can better tailor the content & metadata
   - Double click on the definitions for each of their content asks: what
   do they mean by expert/trainee, what type of screen recordings / coding /
   synthetic data are they looking for? What type of content would qualify as
   complex reasoning? We've taken our best guess in the included sample.
   - Technical / quality specs will also help us arrive at better
   estimates.

To answer your other questions:

   - We feel confident in being able to meet all the content besides
   complex reasoning and MCP. We would need more definition & calibration
   around coding and synthetic data to be sure on those.
   - We price long-form content at an hourly rate and targeted content at a
   per clip rate. Pricing depends on the amount of data the customer is
   licensing now and projected to in the future. Do you have a rough idea of
   their budget?
   - We typically work with customers on a calibration phase and create a
   golden dataset. From there, we can deliver the content in 1 week but this
   is also dependent on the specificity of the client's ask and any labeling
   needs.

Best,

Johnny

subject: Re: [External]Re: [External]Re: [External]Re: [External]Re: Encord <> Thoth AI
text:
Hi Moritz,

Thanks for following up and apologies for the delay in update. As things stand, we are unfortunately still waiting on client feedback to start production. Once we have the green light on that, we are almost certain we would like to work with Encord and would be able to move fast with you to get things set up.

As of now, however, it still doesn't make a lot of sense for us to commit and do anything yet. For our small pilot dataset we used a temporary tool to annotate, which at least gave us a cleaner vision and a lot more insight on the exact functionality and workflows that fit our use case best.

With that there are a lot of new things the arose and we are trying to iron out, so we were wondering if we could ask about them during our scheduled meeting tomorrow? But again, I should just give a disclaimer we won't be able to take your offer just yet.

Please let me know if this is okay with you and if you are still available for a quick chat tomorrow.

Best,
Boris

subject: Re: Post meeting with Ulrik at BD Offices
text:
Hi!
Yes Monday at 11:00 or 11:30 would work.

I followed up with the team and the most important annotation workflows
right now are dense text annotation and selecting and tracking both key
points and masks (with support of SAM 3). A couple people in my team are
working with Abraham on this. We are doing it in the context of a
particular task, but getting to good confidence on the quality and
efficiency in tracking these geometric features is the core thing we need
to scale the annotation jobs to a much larger set of tasks. Happy to talk
more about it on Monday!

Alberto.
